description: Declaration-only ZipDMA F6 behavior that states a two-channel, eight-byte-beat, two-outstanding transfer. The planner must refuse it by name: the pinned ZipDMA has one channel, a 32-bit bus and one outstanding request, and this file is the negative declaration that proves the refusal.
notes: This file is deliberately beyond the selected device. It is not referenced by any scenario that is expected to pass: it exists so the planner's refusal (dma-capability-beyond-device:channels:2>1, then the beat and outstanding facts) is exercised on a real declaration instead of only in a unit test
the transfer geometry is otherwise the same four-word block, so the only reason a run would refuse is the capability block: a refusal that named the block would be a different finding
no execution is claimed: a two-channel or wide-beat transfer cannot be encoded by this RTL, so nothing here is a multi-channel DMA run
